content.content:
1	# Status
2	
3	**Updated:** 2026-10-28
4	
5	Core extraction, resolver, CLI, NAPI binding, and Vite plugin all work and are fully tested. Config file loading, watch mode (including rebuilds on config changes and polling with `ensure_fresh`), plugin architecture, TOON token-optimized output format, JSON schema export, and bounded atomic DTS caching are implemented and verified.
6	
7	**Types from other packages.** Imports resolve to any file under a source directory, `.d.ts` included, so a monorepo whose packages are all source directories resolves across them. By default the declarations those names point to are loaded (ADR 0010): a prop typed by an installed package resolves. `--no-load-dependencies` (config, NAPI and Vite `loadDependencies: false`) reads only `@types/react` and TypeScript's own lib files from `node_modules`, and then a prop whose type comes from any other installed package stays a named reference with an `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` warning. Checked against RDT on five installed repos, loading reports far more of RDT's props and changes 11 matching types in 59,000. Chakra, the worst case, costs about 220 ms and 330 MiB against 50 ms and 100 MiB without (`docs/performance.md`).
8	
9	## Numbers
10	
11	- Rust tests (`cargo nextest` across the workspace, plus the NAPI binding tests) and vitest (unit with a mocked binding, integration against the real native binding), all green in CI
12	- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean with `unsafe_code = "deny"` enforced workspace-wide
13	- 20 real-world fixture libraries validated against `react-docgen-typescript` (shadcn, Radix, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, React Aria, antd, ariakit, ark-ui, base-ui, blueprint, day-picker, fluentui, headlessui, panda, react-final-form, react-resizable-panels, storybook-emotion, tanstack-table, zendesk-garden — see `rdt-coverage.md`)
14	- **Recall** against `react-docgen-typescript` with dependencies installed and loaded (`docs/measurement.md`, 2026-10-23): share of RDT's non-React props reported Mantine 99.7%, Chakra 98.6%, shadcn/ui 39.5%, Ant Design 80.3%, react-spectrum 99.7%.
15	- **Precision** per detection rule (`docs/precision.md`, 2026-10-21): 1 component that isn't one in 154 sampled, `functionDeclaration` 96% and every other rule 100%. 25 samples per rule can't yet establish the 95% gate.
16	- **Speed** on five pinned public corpora (`docs/performance.md`, 2026-10-22): 34 to 81 ms wall time and 66 to 153 MB peak RSS for 41 to 490 kLOC, 17 to 39 times faster than `react-docgen-typescript` on the same files. No pull-request gate enforces it: a weekly workflow records speed, memory and recall against RDT and react-docgen and opens an issue on a worsening, and `just bench` compares a branch with `main` locally (`docs/measurement.md`).
17	
18	## Features and improvements
19	
20	- **`htmlAttributes` defaults to `full`** — every attribute `@types/react` declares is listed, `ref` for `forwardRef` and `ComponentProps<"div">` props; `curated` is an opt-in compact mode. Costs against the old default: wall time +9 to +31%, peak RSS +12 to +37%, canonical JSON +42 to +105%.
21	- **Testing Stack** — `cargo-nextest` process runner, `rstest` parameterized spec tables, `insta` snapshots, and `trycmd` executable Markdown CLI specs.
22	- **Plugin system** (`DocgenPlugin` / `PluginRegistry`) — Extensible AST and component resolution hooks in `crates/core/src/plugin.rs`.
23	- **TOON output format** (`--format toon` / `toon.rs`) — Token-optimized format for LLM agents, cutting context window token usage by ~65-75%.
24	- **JSON schema export** (`caliper-docgen schema`) — Machine-readable Draft-07 JSON Schema export for component metadata validation.
25	- **Atomic & Bounded DTS cache** (`cache.rs`) — Atomic temp-file swap writes, dirty flag tracking, and 5,000 entry eviction cap. Keyed by content hash, and discarded whenever the build that wrote it differs.
26	- **Lazy sessions** (ADR 0016) — `WatchSession::lazy` parses and indexes every file and resolves a component when a request names it; the Storybook addon uses it by default (NAPI `lazy`, off by default). Each answer equals the batch extraction's for the same key. Numbers in `docs/performance.md`.
27	- **Dependency declarations loaded by default** (ADR 0010) — a prop typed by an installed package resolves; `--no-load-dependencies` turns it off.
28	- **Strict Safe Rust** — `unsafe_code = "deny"` via `[workspace.lints]`, active across all three crates (`core`, `cli`, `binding`) — none currently use `unsafe`, including the NAPI FFI boundary (napi-rs's `#[napi]` macros generate the glue without user-visible `unsafe`).
29	
30	## Known gaps that won't get fixed without a type checker
31	
32	See the "Known gaps summary" table in `rdt-coverage.md` for the full, maintained list. The short version: conditional types that need inference (`infer`, an unbound generic), mapped types over an unbound generic, and a couple of `@emotion/styled`-specific call shapes all need real type inference OXC deliberately doesn't do. Not bugs. A conditional, indexed access or mapped type whose operands are known is evaluated (`resolver/evaluate.rs`).
33	
34	An opt-in TypeScript 7 semantic backend is implemented as slice 1 (ADR 0006, ADR 0007), experimental and off by default: `extract --experimental-semantic-types`, see `type-checker-integration.md`. Accuracy is verified against real RDT — 0 missing/extra props on 13 hand-picked components, and re-verified on `7.1.0-beta` against the full 44-file fixture corpus (5,508/5,522 `required` matches, 5,266/5,522 type-string matches; the gap is explained noise, not a resolver bug) — and the RDT oracle that comparison depends on now runs on its own `typescript@6` install, separate from the semantic probe's `typescript@7.1.0-beta`. TypeScript 7.1's checker also runs, test-only, as an oracle for structural prop types (`docs/measurement.md`). A session can also ask a warm checker for just the component a story requests (`semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`, ADR 0022): the first answer waits up to `semanticWaitMs` (default 150) and takes the structural props if the checker is slower, and the checker's late answer is kept for the next request. It needs `typescript@7.1.0-beta` (the pinned version) or `tscPath`, and is experimental and off by default. A missing, crashed or timed-out `tsc` falls back to the structural result with one warning; the open lifecycle items are in `type-checker-integration.md`'s Gates table.
35	
36	## Experiments that didn't pan out
37

# Status

**Updated:** 2026-10-28

Core extraction, resolver, CLI, NAPI binding, and Vite plugin all work and are fully tested. Config file loading, watch mode (including rebuilds on config changes and polling with `ensure_fresh`), plugin architecture, TOON token-optimized output format, JSON schema export, and bounded atomic DTS caching are implemented and verified.

**Types from other packages.** Imports resolve to any file under a source directory, `.d.ts` included, so a monorepo whose packages are all source directories resolves across them. By default the declarations those names point to are loaded (ADR 0010): a prop typed by an installed package resolves. `--no-load-dependencies` (config, NAPI and Vite `loadDependencies: false`) reads only `@types/react` and TypeScript's own lib files from `node_modules`, and then a prop whose type comes from any other installed package stays a named reference with an `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` warning. Checked against RDT on five installed repos, loading reports far more of RDT's props and changes 11 matching types in 59,000. Chakra, the worst case, costs about 220 ms and 330 MiB against 50 ms and 100 MiB without (`docs/performance.md`).

## Numbers

- Rust tests (`cargo nextest` across the workspace, plus the NAPI binding tests) and vitest (unit with a mocked binding, integration against the real native binding), all green in CI
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean with `unsafe_code = "deny"` enforced workspace-wide
- 20 real-world fixture libraries validated against `react-docgen-typescript` (shadcn, Radix, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, React Aria, antd, ariakit, ark-ui, base-ui, blueprint, day-picker, fluentui, headlessui, panda, react-final-form, react-resizable-panels, storybook-emotion, tanstack-table, zendesk-garden — see `rdt-coverage.md`)
- **Recall** against `react-docgen-typescript` with dependencies installed and loaded (`docs/measurement.md`, 2026-10-23): share of RDT's non-React props reported Mantine 99.7%, Chakra 98.6%, shadcn/ui 39.5%, Ant Design 80.3%, react-spectrum 99.7%.
- **Precision** per detection rule (`docs/precision.md`, 2026-10-21): 1 component that isn't one in 154 sampled, `functionDeclaration` 96% and every other rule 100%. 25 samples per rule can't yet establish the 95% gate.
- **Speed** on five pinned public corpora (`docs/performance.md`, 2026-10-22): 34 to 81 ms wall time and 66 to 153 MB peak RSS for 41 to 490 kLOC, 17 to 39 times faster than `react-docgen-typescript` on the same files. No pull-request gate enforces it: a weekly workflow records speed, memory and recall against RDT and react-docgen and opens an issue on a worsening, and `just bench` compares a branch with `main` locally (`docs/measurement.md`).

## Features and improvements

- **`htmlAttributes` defaults to `full`** — every attribute `@types/react` declares is listed, `ref` for `forwardRef` and `ComponentProps<"div">` props; `curated` is an opt-in compact mode. Costs against the old default: wall time +9 to +31%, peak RSS +12 to +37%, canonical JSON +42 to +105%.
- **Testing Stack** — `cargo-nextest` process runner, `rstest` parameterized spec tables, `insta` snapshots, and `trycmd` executable Markdown CLI specs.
- **Plugin system** (`DocgenPlugin` / `PluginRegistry`) — Extensible AST and component resolution hooks in `crates/core/src/plugin.rs`.
- **TOON output format** (`--format toon` / `toon.rs`) — Token-optimized format for LLM agents, cutting context window token usage by ~65-75%.
- **JSON schema export** (`caliper-docgen schema`) — Machine-readable Draft-07 JSON Schema export for component metadata validation.
- **Atomic & Bounded DTS cache** (`cache.rs`) — Atomic temp-file swap writes, dirty flag tracking, and 5,000 entry eviction cap. Keyed by content hash, and discarded whenever the build that wrote it differs.
- **Lazy sessions** (ADR 0016) — `WatchSession::lazy` parses and indexes every file and resolves a component when a request names it; the Storybook addon uses it by default (NAPI `lazy`, off by default). Each answer equals the batch extraction's for the same key. Numbers in `docs/performance.md`.
- **Dependency declarations loaded by default** (ADR 0010) — a prop typed by an installed package resolves; `--no-load-dependencies` turns it off.
- **Strict Safe Rust** — `unsafe_code = "deny"` via `[workspace.lints]`, active across all three crates (`core`, `cli`, `binding`) — none currently use `unsafe`, including the NAPI FFI boundary (napi-rs's `#[napi]` macros generate the glue without user-visible `unsafe`).

## Known gaps that won't get fixed without a type checker

See the "Known gaps summary" table in `rdt-coverage.md` for the full, maintained list. The short version: conditional types that need inference (`infer`, an unbound generic), mapped types over an unbound generic, and a couple of `@emotion/styled`-specific call shapes all need real type inference OXC deliberately doesn't do. Not bugs. A conditional, indexed access or mapped type whose operands are known is evaluated (`resolver/evaluate.rs`).

An opt-in TypeScript 7 semantic backend is implemented as slice 1 (ADR 0006, ADR 0007), experimental and off by default: `extract --experimental-semantic-types`, see `type-checker-integration.md`. Accuracy is verified against real RDT — 0 missing/extra props on 13 hand-picked components, and re-verified on `7.1.0-beta` against the full 44-file fixture corpus (5,508/5,522 `required` matches, 5,266/5,522 type-string matches; the gap is explained noise, not a resolver bug) — and the RDT oracle that comparison depends on now runs on its own `typescript@6` install, separate from the semantic probe's `typescript@7.1.0-beta`. TypeScript 7.1's checker also runs, test-only, as an oracle for structural prop types (`docs/measurement.md`). A session can also ask a warm checker for just the component a story requests (`semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`, ADR 0022): the first answer waits up to `semanticWaitMs` (default 150) and takes the structural props if the checker is slower, and the checker's late answer is kept for the next request. It needs `typescript@7.1.0-beta` (the pinned version) or `tscPath`, and is experimental and off by default. A missing, crashed or timed-out `tsc` falls back to the structural result with one warning; the open lifecycle items are in `type-checker-integration.md`'s Gates table.

## Experiments that didn't pan out

**Confidence routing (2026-10-25).** The idea: score each component's risk of wrong or missing props from Caliper's own output, and ask the TypeScript 7.1 checker only about the risky ones. Measured against the checker on 518,268 shared props over the five corpora and the fixtures, routing 10% of components caught 23% of the props only the checker reports with the existing warning rule (a component with a degrade warning or error), against 3% for a smoothed table and 6% for a logistic model. At a 20% budget neither model caught the one prop the oracle marks `wrong`. Most of the checker-only props were Next's ambient augmentation (1,154 of 1,182 on shadcn) or false component matches, which a score of structural risk can't learn. So no score ships: warnings stay the signal, and on-demand checker use asks about the requested component instead of predicting. The script was deleted; the method is the oracle in `docs/measurement.md` plus the numbers above.

## Where to look next

- **Open gaps** → `edge-cases.md` — the gaps still open. Add one when you find a gap you aren't fixing now; delete it when you fix it.
- **What broke and why, historically** → `rdt-coverage.md` — every bug found during real-library validation, root cause, and the fix. Keep this updated; it's the project's memory.
- **Why a hard-to-reverse decision was made** → `docs/adr/` — OXC over the TypeScript compiler, manual serde for `PropType`, positional msgpack encoding, panic containment, the TypeScript 7 semantic backend. Write a new one when you make a decision like these (see `docs/adr/README.md`).
- **How the pipeline fits together** → `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (moved from `.claude/semantic-model/` so every coding agent can read it, not just Claude Code — `AGENTS.md` is now this repo's shared instructions file, with per-tool mirrors under `.codex/`, `.cursor/`, `.gemini/`, `.github/`, `.opencode/`).
- **Setup, testing, code style, commit conventions** → `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- **Migrating from react-docgen-typescript** → `MIGRATING.md`

# Edge cases and known gaps

Gaps that are still open. The 2026-08-04 audit that this file used to record (crash and hang risks, silent data loss, silent wrong output; 43 fixes) has landed; its findings are in git history (`git log --follow docs/edge-cases.md`) and each fix has a regression test. Bugs found by real-library validation are in `rdt-coverage.md`. Type-inference gaps are in `type-checker-integration.md`.

Add an entry when you find a gap you are not fixing now. Delete it when you fix it.

## Detection

- Wrapper calls with no type argument are not recognized: `createIconLoader('x')`, `lazy(() => import(...))`, `createIcon({...})`. Reading the props needs the call's return type, which the structural path doesn't have. The opt-in TypeScript backend (ADR 0006) can.
- Some components are reported under a different name than `react-docgen-typescript` uses: `displayName` assignments, and compound members such as `Tabs.List`.

## Resolution

- Mapped types, conditional types and indexed access over an unbound generic, and `@emotion/styled`'s two-argument overload, need real type inference. They degrade to `Opaque` with a diagnostic and, where possible, a `composes` entry. See `type-checker-integration.md`.
- Ambient globals (`lib.dom.d.ts` and the like) are looked up from `options.src_dirs.first()` only (`pipeline/mod.rs`, `pipeline/revision.rs`). If the first source directory can't resolve `typescript` but a later one could, ambient lookups return nothing for the whole run. Untested against a real multi-root config.

## Output

- TOON is lossy on purpose: unions and intersections print at most 4 members, literal unions at most 6, each followed by `...(+N)`. The module doc of `toon.rs` doesn't say so.

New `apps/oracle/src/tool-norm.ts`: RDT type object and react-docgen `tsType.raw` to the oracle's Norm form through one TS-string mapper. `scripts/rdt.mjs:31` currently keeps only the string "enum" for enum props (4 to 5% of own props); change it to keep the type object and only own props. react-docgen default resolver throws on 17 to 21% of files; record the failed count. Docs claim react-docgen reads files alone, but it follows relative imports (verified): fix the wording in `scripts/rdg.mjs` and `docs/measurement.md`. A scratch prototype of both adapters gave sensible verdicts on 27 fixture props.
- `oracle/three-tools-report` (stacked). `apps/oracle/src/oracle.ts` takes `--rdt` and `--rdg` dumps; `scripts/weekly.py` passes them; `entry['oracle']` keeps Caliper's `shared_props/agree/wrong` for continuity and adds `tools`. Cost about +5 to 15 s on the weekly Measure step (inferred). Edits `weekly.py`, so land the pairing branches first.
- Optional later: `oracle/default-and-description` (defaults and descriptions are not checker truth; label as such).
Known risks: rules validated only on antd and shadcn (Mantine, Chakra, Spectrum are not installed locally; validate from a CI weekly run on the branch); `excluded_sample` should be read on the other corpora; the 7.1 checker is a beta and some "wrong" verdicts may be the oracle's own (spectrum 1.09%).

### Trail 2. Resolve faster with dependencies loaded
Acceptance: shadcn `--load-dependencies --no-cache` back to within 5% of the Monday numbers (141 ms, 275 MiB locally; weekly CI within 10% of the Monday record); extract output byte-identical; the watch and lazy tests in `crates/core/tests/react_augmentation_watch.rs` stay green; each branch states its measured delta.
Measured causes (local, shadcn, uncontended, median of 7 to 11; toggles disabled together restored 148 to 150 ms and 280 MiB): derived `Ord` on `Demand` sorts on the identical `from` path first (about 10 ms serial); module-only demands add resolution (about 10 ms) plus 64-file augmentation scans that parse and retain about 580 files (+50 MiB); the per-attribute-read `react_augmentations` lookup (77k calls per run, about 5.5 ms). `members` copying and JSON size are negligible (measured delta zero).
Branches:
- `perf/project-demands-sort` (main). `crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs`. Sort by (specifier, name) only. About 10 ms on shadcn, no RSS change.
- `perf/cache-react-augmentations` (main). `named_type_index.rs`, `resolver/html.rs`, `resolver/deps.rs`. Compute the augmenting-file list once per index layer chain and memoize per (react_file, key) inside the index (rebuilt per revision, never a static); record the file list as one slice and return early when the recorder already holds `reads_augmentations`. About 4 to 5 ms.
- `perf/module-demands-lean` (stacked on the sort branch; same file). Resolve module-only demands once per (specifier, nearest package.json directory), skip specifiers that resolve into the project, replace the full `parse_file` in `find_augmenting_files` with a light pass, retain nothing for files that are neither augmenting nor re-exporting. About 5 ms and -50 MiB. Do not pre-filter by package.json `react` dependency (decision 5).
- `perf/dependency-parse-cache` (throwaway prototype; decide from the numbers).
- `perf/members-shared-list`: skip (zero measured effect); hygiene only.
Hard constraint: Revision::affected_by (`pipeline/revision.rs` about lines 120 to 126) re-resolves a component when `change.react_namespace && depends_on.reads_augmentations` or the changed file is in `depends_on.files`; any caching must keep that true.

### Trail 3. Detect components by shape and import source
Acceptance: `FC`, `ComponentType`, `FunctionComponent`, `Component`, `PureComponent` are matched through a `react` or `preact/compat` import under any alias or namespace (`R.FC`), and a same-named type from another module is not; `const Button = Inner` and `memo(Inner)` resolve even when `Inner` is declared later; exact-content tests; no precision regression; the 211 noise `SKIPPED_CANDIDATE` diagnostics (48 antd, 163 shadcn) go away.
Branches (stacked, same files):
- `fix/react-type-import-source` (main). `extractor/component.rs`, `extractor/mod.rs` (share one helper with `react_api` / `may_be_react`). Fixture-verified: 3 false negatives and 2 false positives, 0 hits in the corpora.
- `fix/alias-resolution-order` (stacked). Defer `try_rename_identifier_wrapped_component` to `finish()`; make the alias-variant matches in `resolver/html.rs` (about lines 83 to 87 and 128 to 132) and `resolver/callee.rs` (about 183 to 214) exhaustive.

### Trail 4. Find the components we still miss
Acceptance: each new rule is by shape, never by library name; each has a precision sample (`scripts/precision-sample.py`, 25 per rule; the gate is 95%); every `SourceData` shape change appends fields at the end and bumps `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` (ADR 0003), so the branches are strictly sequential; `just bench` and a dependency-loaded shadcn and Chakra measurement for time and peak RSS; object-literal members and dependency re-exports stay out (decisions 1 and 2).
Branches (one stack on trail 3's tip):
- `feat/imported-destructure-alias`. `const { Option } = Imported` and `const X = ImportedIdent` through the existing ImportedMemberAlias machinery; drop when it resolves to a project component of the same name. +1 antd, +4 shadcn (ChartLegend x4), and about 20 antd noise skips removed.
- `feat/factory-results`. `FunctionResult` for const-bound arrows with type parameters and for functions that return a rendering function; `return Local` with `Local = X as T`. +5 shadcn (IconLucide family), +1 antd (Calendar). DatePicker is not expected.
- `feat/cross-file-render-evidence`. Keep declined typed-props candidates; promote one when a project file imports and renders it. +1 antd (QRcodeStatus); shadcn `GET` must stay declined.
Known caution: the first analysis reported antd factory-built components as 6 real misses; only Calendar (+1) is expected to be recoverable. About 8 of the 55 shadcn misses are naming mismatches Caliper already covers (RDT `Tooltip` vs `ChartTooltip`): fix those in trail 1's pairing, not in the extractor.

### Trail 5. Types Storybook and agents can trust
Acceptance: the parity report separates defects from deliberate differences; each verified defect has an exact-content test and the oracle agree rate does not fall; prop-level degradation reason is in canonical output (a new optional field is not a schema bump) and TOON; a 20-question deterministic agent evaluation runs in the weekly job and reports silent-wrong answers (issue when above 0 or when correct drops 5 points); a narrow NAPI slice view exists.
Measured at main 53970b80 (parity harness, 110 shadcn and 84 antd sampled stories): props Storybook lists that we lack: shadcn 0, antd 14 in 2 stories (one verified defect: the rest probably a harness name collision); 14,795 of 14,800 shadcn extras are HTML attributes (deliberate; `htmlAttributes: none` cuts them to 5); shared props 338 and 1,315, same type text 58.3% and 67.4% (heuristic normaliser, about 68 and 160 unreviewed in "other"); real defects about 6% of shared props (defaults from dependency `defaultProps`, unresolved indexed access and `keyof typeof`, wrong `required`); degraded rate 4.8% and 4.0% (docs say 42.1% and 27.4% from 2026-10-24: not explained); antd, none attributes: 4.8% of prop instances are bare Named, 18 Opaque, 135 of 251 components carry an affecting diagnostic; TOON is about 7x smaller than canonical (antd 471 KB vs 3.4 MB) but has no NAPI route and drops provenance.
Branches:
- `feat/parity-detail-report` (main). `packages/storybook/scripts/storybook-parity.mjs`, `docs/storybook-parity.md`.
- `fix/trust-defects-batch` (main; run `just bench`). `crates/core/src/resolver/`, `pipeline/rdt.rs`: `PropsWithChildren<T>` children (Masonry), `keyof typeof` and `typeof X` in unions (Result.status, Cascader), indexed access on generic base-ui props, wrong `required` for an optional base and a required override (Segmented.options), collapse `undefined | boolean` to boolean, flag non-literal default expressions.
- `feat/prop-level-confidence` (main). `toon.rs`, `types/output.rs`, `crates/binding/src/`, `packages/napi/index.d.ts`: attach the degradation reason to the prop; TOON quotes literal unions, prints layer members and a source column; then the narrow NAPI slice view.
- `feat/agent-eval-weekly` (stacked after trail 1: it edits `weekly.py`). `scripts/agent_eval.py`, `scripts/agent_questions.json`, `scripts/test_agent_eval.py`.

### Trail 6. A complete release flow
Acceptance: each version produces one GitHub Release for `cargo/caliper-docgen` with notes; CLI binaries attached with build attestations; recovery through `callisto release pending` plus the drain job and a scheduled check; `callisto release --dry-run` in the PR check; the first real release verified from its receipt and the providers.
Facts: Callisto 0.16.0 (2026-10-28) is the latest and is what we pin. Our `callisto.toml` `publish-to` lists only crates.io and npm, so Callisto pushes tags and publishes packages but creates no GitHub Releases; `publish-to` accepts `"github-release"`; binaries need a `[release]` section (`product-package`, `forge-repository`, one `[[release.artifact]]` per target with `asset-name`); `release.yml` currently asserts zero artifact slots. Callisto's own worked example (`orin-dx/callisto` `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, 10 jobs against our 6) also has `recovery-checks` and `drain` jobs (`release pending`, finish the oldest unfinished release, then refresh the release PR), `actions/attest`, and a schedule trigger. Docs: `docs/releasing.md`, `docs/config.md` in that repo. A failed release is re-selected on every main push and holds back the release PR refresh. One run (the #274 push) failed at "Create or update the Callisto release PR" and recovered on the next push; cause not found. The tap reads tags and is unaffected.
Branches (stacked, all edit `release.yml` or `callisto.toml`): GitHub Releases with notes; binaries and attestations; recovery and schedule. Do not edit while a release is in flight.

## Order, sessions, concurrency

- Wave 0 (coordinator): create the six trails with the acceptance criteria above; write the branch table into each trail body; nothing else.
- Wave 1 in parallel: trail 1 and trail 2 (no shared files).
- Wave 2: trail 3 then trail 4 as one stacked lineage (serial); trail 5's independent branches once trail 1's weekly changes land; `agent-eval-weekly` last. Trail 6 after the in-flight release finishes.
- One session per trail. A session may fan out a workflow (isolated worktrees, schema'd results, an adversarial review stage) for independent branches; stacked branches are done in order. Agent teams are experimental and untried here: try one trail with a team before adopting.
- A coordinator session owns merge order, conflicts, the weekly rerun after merges and the trail bodies. Workers never merge or edit another trail.
- About three live sessions at most (separate `target` dirs, CPU contention; profiling must run alone).

## Process (rules that cost real incidents)

- Plan before create: trails and the branch table first, then branches. Do not create one trail per PR. A change cannot be reparented to another trail once it belongs to one (409), and the CLI has no delete.
- Link-first flow (recorded in memory `plan-trails-before-branches.md`): create the trail intent-only; push the branch; `entire trail link <n> --branch <b> --base <base>` (set `--base` to the parent branch for stacked branches, before any PR exists); Entire opens the PR; edit its title and body keeping the `entire-shadow-pr` marker. Linking a stacked branch after a PR already exists made Entire open a duplicate main-based PR (#277, #278); avoid.
- Merging: `entire trail merge` merges one change into its base through the trail's gates (approvals, CI, base CI, up to date) and never merges a trail's other changes; not yet tried here, test on a low-stakes PR. Merge stacks bottom-up; never merge a child into its parent's branch (that stranded #275's merge commit; the content was saved only because Entire's main-based duplicate #278 merged first). After a parent merges, retarget the child to `main` and merge `main` into it (no rebase, no force-push).
- Before any push run the whole CI set, not a subset of crates: `CI=1 CALIPER_TEST_TSC=<worktree>/apps/oracle/node_modules/typescript-beta/bin/tsc cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked`, `just lint doc-check typos machete`, and the TypeScript package tests if `packages/` changed. A missed CLI-crate literal broke #271 once. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in each worktree (snapshots need node_modules). Resolver changes also need `just bench` and a dependency-loaded shadcn run for time and RSS.
- Commits are GPG-signed (check `git log -1 --format='%h %G?'` prints G; use /usr/bin/git, one plain command per call, sandbox off for git writes). Never `--no-gpg-sign`, never force-push, never push to main.
- PR bodies: succinct, what changed, why, measured numbers, risks, the trail URL, the session URL last.
- Directly opened PRs use `gh pr create` (the global shim runs it as the PR bot and needs Touch ID; batch them). The global guard hook blocks commands that mention the bot's credentials; do not read `~/.config/orin-dx` or `~/Library/Application Support/OrinDX-PR-Bot`.
- Changesets: one short consumer paragraph, starting with the outcome; none for scripts-only changes.

## Tracking with Entire (from its help text; mostly untried)

- Worker start: `entire trail checkout <n> --worktree` then `entire trail resume <n>` (restores the checkpoint sessions on the trail branch and starts the agent with the trail's context).
- Coordinator: `entire session list`, `entire session tokens`, `entire trail watch <n>`, `entire dispatch`.
- Reviews: Entire's agent review runs on each PR; read it with `entire trail finding <repo>/<change> --project gh/orin-dx --freshness any --json`; the worker fixes verified findings. Findings, not comments, for agent feedback.
- Keep each trail body current with `entire trail update <n> --body ...` as branches land. Trail commands need the sandbox off (keychain and network).

## Unknowns to settle early

- Storybook's real react-docgen resolver configuration (decision 3).
- Why spectrum's oracle wrong-rate is 1.09% and shadcn's 0.08% (appeared between the baseline and the Monday run).
- Why the parity harness's degraded rate (4.8%, 4.0%) differs from the 2026-10-24 docs (42.1%, 27.4%).
- Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum behaviour for every new rule (not installed locally; use the CI weekly run on a branch).
- False-positive rate of every new detection rule except the 19 object-literal members measured.
- Release flow decisions for trail 6 (product package, binaries, attestations).

## Start prompts

Coordinator session:
> Read /Users/gabe/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/plan/next-trails-2026-11-02.md in full, then the memory note plan-trails-before-branches.md. You are the coordinator. Do Wave 0 only: create the six trails intent-only with the acceptance criteria and branch tables from the plan, confirm the trail numbers back to me, and wait. Do not create branches or PRs.

Worker session (replace N and the trail name):
> Read /Users/gabe/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/plan/next-trails-2026-11-02.md (the section for trail N and the Process section) and run `entire trail show N`. You own trail N only. Follow the plan's branch table, link-first flow and CI checklist. Fan out independent branches with a workflow in isolated worktrees; do stacked branches in order. Report numbers against the baselines in the plan. Update the trail body as branches land. Do not merge, and do not touch other trails' files.

**How to apply:**
1. Write the plan first: trail title and acceptance criteria, then each branch (name, base, stacked or independent, files it touches, owner). Decide stack vs parallel by file overlap. Get a yes.
2. Create the trails (intent-only, `entire trail create --no-branch`), then branches, then open every PR in one batch so one Touch ID approval covers them.

content.content:
Create a repository-scoped project trail, then link its branch. In the current repository, publish the local branch first; no separate commit or push is required. Uses the current feature branch, or derives a new branch from the title when on the base branch. Use --branch to choose a branch, or --no-branch for intent only. With --no-branch, the current or --repo repository becomes the Trail scope and requires repository write access; --project without --repo creates unscoped intent instead. Repository writers can create scoped trails and link branches. Unscoped creation requires project management. With a branch, --idempotency-key applies only to linking; if linking fails, retry with trail link rather than creating another trail. With --repo, no local branch is published: link existing remote work or use --branch-action create to create it on the server from --base. This command does not commit changes or change the local checkout. Branches are preserved if creation fails.

Usage:
  entire trail create [flags]

Flags:
      --assignee strings         Assignee logins; replaces the complete list (--assignee= clears it)
      --base string              Base branch for new code work
      --body string              Trail description (--body= clears it on update)
      --branch string            Branch to use (defaults to the current feature branch; create derives one from the title on the base branch)
      --branch-action string     Branch action: link existing remote work, or create a new branch (default "link")
  -h, --help                     help for create
      --idempotency-key string   Retry key for linking a branch; with intent-only creation, requires project management
      --json                     Output raw JSON instead of a table
      --no-branch                Create intent scoped to the current or --repo repository; --project alone creates unscoped intent
      --priority string          Priority (urgent, high, medium, low, none)
      --status string            Lifecycle status (open, closed)
      --title string             Trail title
      --type string              Type (bug, feature, task)

Global Flags:
      --context name     Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
      --project string   Project as gh/<owner> or et/<project>; required for list, otherwise defaults to the repository's namespace
      --repo string      Target repository as forge/owner/repo (e.g. gh/acme/app) or a clone URL; for list, only filters the required --project
trail list requires --project gh/<owner> or et/<project>; --repo is only a filter within that project

input.command:
D=$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp; mkdir -p $D
cat > $D/t1.md <<'EOF'
## Goal
Compare Caliper, RDT and react-docgen honestly and repeatably. The TypeScript 7.1 checker is the ground truth.

## Acceptance criteria
- antd component recall about 95% with the new pairing (replayed 186/195 strict, 186/194 keeping today's any-call unwrap); shadcn unchanged at 96.5% (none of its 55 unmatched are pairing cases).
- weekly.json records unmatched entries by cause and a `reference_version`; `findings()` skips recall comparison across different reference versions.
- The oracle scores Caliper, RDT and react-docgen with the same rules and shows universe-based agree, missing by declaration stratum, and react-docgen thrown files as their own column.
- Caliper's historical oracle numbers do not change.

## Branches
| Branch | Base | Files / scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fix/weekly-pairing | main | scripts/weekly.py, test_weekly.py, test_weekly_review.py, docs/measurement.md. Same-file default aliases, displayName; unwrap Object.assign/as/satisfies/!/dotted wrappers/alias chains; guards against wrong pairs |
| feat/weekly-unmatched-record | fix/weekly-pairing (stacked) | per-cause counts plus capped lists (~30 KB for five corpora) |
| fix/weekly-caliper-key-collisions | stacked, optional | +1 antd splitter/Panel.tsx |
| oracle/function-marker-rule | main | apps/oracle/src/oracle-compare.ts: `(kp.optional && !cp.optional) \|\| (kp.rest && !cp.rest)`; Caliper numbers must not change |
| oracle/tool-adapters | oracle/function-marker-rule (stacked) | new apps/oracle/src/tool-norm.ts; scripts/rdt.mjs keeps type object and only own props; record react-docgen failed count; fix docs wording that react-docgen reads files alone |
| oracle/three-tools-report | stacked | oracle.ts takes --rdt/--rdg; weekly.py passes them; entry['oracle'] keeps Caliper fields, adds `tools`. Land pairing branches first (edits weekly.py) |
| oracle/default-and-description | optional, later | label defaults/descriptions as not checker truth |

## Risks
Rules validated only on antd and shadcn; validate Mantine/Chakra/Spectrum from a CI weekly run on the branch. The 7.1 checker is a beta; some "wrong" verdicts may be the oracle's own (spectrum 1.09%).

Plan: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/plan/next-trails-2026-11-02.md
EOF
cat > $D/t2.md <<'EOF'
## Goal
Resolve faster with dependencies loaded, without changing output.

## Acceptance criteria
- shadcn `--load-dependencies --no-cache` back within 5% of the Monday numbers (141 ms, 275 MiB locally; weekly CI within 10% of the Monday record).
- extract output byte-identical.
- watch and lazy tests in crates/core/tests/react_augmentation_watch.rs stay green.
- each branch states its measured delta.

## Measured causes (local, shadcn)
Derived `Ord` on `Demand` sorts on the identical `from` path first (~10 ms); module-only demands add resolution (~10 ms) plus 64-file augmentation scans that parse and retain ~580 files (+50 MiB); per-attribute-read `react_augmentations` lookup (77k calls, ~5.5 ms).

## Branches
| Branch | Base | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| perf/project-demands-sort | main | crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs: sort by (specifier, name); ~10 ms |
| perf/cache-react-augmentations | main | named_type_index.rs, resolver/html.rs, resolver/deps.rs: compute augmenting-file list once per index layer chain, memoize per (react_file, key) inside the index; ~4-5 ms |
| perf/module-demands-lean | perf/project-demands-sort (stacked) | resolve module-only demands once per (specifier, package.json dir), skip project-resolving specifiers, light pass instead of full parse_file; ~5 ms, -50 MiB. No pre-filter by package.json `react` |
| perf/dependency-parse-cache | throwaway prototype | decide from measurement (touches ADRs 0003, 0008, 0011) |
| perf/members-shared-list | skip | zero measured effect |

Hard constraint: Revision::affected_by (pipeline/revision.rs) must still re-resolve when `change.react_namespace && depends_on.reads_augmentations` or the changed file is in `depends_on.files`.

Plan: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/plan/next-trails-2026-11-02.md
EOF
cat > $D/t3.md <<'EOF'
## Goal
Detect components by shape and import source.

## Acceptance criteria
- `FC`, `ComponentType`, `FunctionComponent`, `Component`, `PureComponent` match through a `react` or `preact/compat` import under any alias or namespace (`R.FC`); a same-named type from another module does not.
- `const Button = Inner` and `memo(Inner)` resolve even when `Inner` is declared later.
- exact-content tests; no precision regression.
- the 211 noise SKIPPED_CANDIDATE diagnostics (48 antd, 163 shadcn) go away.

## Branches (stacked, same files)
| Branch | Base | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fix/react-type-import-source | main | extractor/component.rs, extractor/mod.rs; share one helper with react_api / may_be_react |
| fix/alias-resolution-order | fix/react-type-import-source (stacked) | defer try_rename_identifier_wrapped_component to finish(); make alias-variant matches in resolver/html.rs and resolver/callee.rs exhaustive |

Plan: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/plan/next-trails-2026-11-02.md
EOF
cat > $D/t4.md <<'EOF'
## Goal
Find the components Caliper still misses, by shape never by library name.

## Acceptance criteria
- each new rule has a precision sample (scripts/precision-sample.py, 25 per rule; gate 95%).
- every `SourceData` shape change appends fields at the end and bumps CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION (ADR 0003), so branches are strictly sequential.
- `just bench` plus dependency-loaded shadcn and Chakra measurement for time and peak RSS.
- object-literal members and dependency re-exports stay out.

## Branches (one stack on trail 3's tip)
| Branch | Base | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| feat/imported-destructure-alias | trail 3 tip | `const { Option } = Imported`, `const X = ImportedIdent` via ImportedMemberAlias; +1 antd, +4 shadcn, ~20 antd noise skips removed |
| feat/factory-results | previous (stacked) | FunctionResult for const-bound arrows with type params and render-function returns; +5 shadcn, +1 antd (Calendar) |
| feat/cross-file-render-evidence | previous (stacked) | promote a declined typed-props candidate when a project file imports and renders it; +1 antd; shadcn GET stays declined |

Caution: only Calendar is expected recoverable of antd factory-built components. ~8 of 55 shadcn misses are naming mismatches fixed in trail 1's pairing.

Plan: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/plan/next-trails-2026-11-02.md
EOF
cat > $D/t5.md <<'EOF'
## Goal
Types Storybook and in-process agents can trust.

## Acceptance criteria
- parity report separates defects from deliberate differences; each verified defect has an exact-content test and oracle agree rate does not fall.
- prop-level degradation reason in canonical output (new optional field, not a schema bump) and TOON.
- 20-question deterministic agent evaluation runs in the weekly job and reports silent-wrong answers (issue when above 0 or correct drops 5 points).
- a narrow NAPI slice view exists.

## Branches
| Branch | Base | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| feat/parity-detail-report | main | packages/storybook/scripts/storybook-parity.mjs, docs/storybook-parity.md |
| fix/trust-defects-batch | main (run just bench) | resolver/, pipeline/rdt.rs: PropsWithChildren<T> children, keyof typeof / typeof X in unions, indexed access on generic base-ui props, wrong `required` (Segmented.options), undefined\|boolean, non-literal defaults |
| feat/prop-level-confidence | main | toon.rs, types/output.rs, crates/binding/src, packages/napi/index.d.ts: degradation reason on prop; TOON literal unions, layer members, source column; then narrow NAPI slice view |
| feat/agent-eval-weekly | stacked after trail 1 (edits weekly.py) | scripts/agent_eval.py, agent_questions.json, test_agent_eval.py |

Plan: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/plan/next-trails-2026-11-02.md
EOF
cat > $D/t6.md <<'EOF'
## Goal
A complete release flow publishing GitHub Releases.

## Acceptance criteria
- each version produces one GitHub Release for `cargo/caliper-docgen` with notes.
- CLI binaries attached with build attestations.
- recovery through `callisto release pending` plus a drain job and a scheduled check.
- `callisto release --dry-run` in the PR check.
- the first real release verified from its receipt and the providers.

## Branches (stacked; all edit release.yml / callisto.toml)
| Branch | Base | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub Releases with notes | main | add "github-release" to publish-to |
| Binaries and attestations | previous (stacked) | [release] section, [[release.artifact]] per target, actions/attest |
| Recovery and schedule | previous (stacked) | recovery-checks and drain jobs, schedule trigger, dry-run in PR check |

Not yet answered by the user: product package (`cargo/caliper-docgen`), attached binaries, attestations. Verify before starting. Do not edit while a release is in flight.

Plan: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/plan/next-trails-2026-11-02.md
EOF
ls $D
input.description: Write six trail body files

  Project: gh/orin-dx

Description:
## Goal
Find the components Caliper still misses, by shape never by library name.

## Acceptance criteria
- each new rule has a precision sample (scripts/precision-sample.py, 25 per rule; gate 95%).
- every `SourceData` shape change appends fields at the end and bumps CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION (ADR 0003), so branches are strictly sequential.
- `just bench` plus dependency-loaded shadcn and Chakra measurement for time and peak RSS.
- object-literal members and dependency re-exports stay out.

## Numbers against the plan's baselines

I replayed the weekly measurement locally on the pinned antd and shadcn corpora with the `main` binary. The baseline replay matches the plan's weekly run exactly (antd 165/207, shadcn 1518/1573).

| Corpus | Components before | Components after |

| antd | 165/207 = 79.7% | 186/202 = 92.1% |

- **Matches the plan:** the antd numerator of 186 is the plan's figure. Own props with layers moved 99.3% to 99.4%.
- **Misses the plan:** the plan expected a denominator of about 195, and this change reaches 202. I could not reproduce the plan's 7 extra merges. The 16 antd items still unpaired are not pairing cases:
  - 6 are `generate*` factory functions and helpers.
  - 4 are `Parent.Member` entries that Caliper reports under the parent, such as `Form.List` and `Mentions.Option`.
  - 2 are the calendar and date-picker components, built by a factory call.
  - 3 are `confirm`, `RefIcon` and `InternalPanel`.
  - 1 is `List`, and 1 is `QrcodeStatus`, which is trail 4's work.
- **To reach about 95%:** you would have to drop compound members from the reference, which hides a gap that `docs/edge-cases.md` lists. I did not do that.

  - **Guards:** the RDT name must be the file's or directory's own, and a Caliper key that another RDT entry already matches is never a target.
  - **`reference_version`:** the record gains `reference_version` (2). `findings()` skips recall when the two records' versions differ, and the summary says so.

Risks: same-file pairing is guarded (RDT name must be the file's or directory's own; a key another entry matches exactly is never a target) but checked only on antd and shadcn. content.text:
The failed release run (41469894346, the push at 15:16Z on `85b639d7`) hit a race in the "Create or update the Callisto release PR" step. It was not a real release failure, and the runs after it all succeeded, including the latest, 41485334016.

Callisto stopped with `E148: release PR snapshot changed after Callisto made its decision` and made no forge changes. It had planned the 0.8.0 → 0.9.0 bump from one snapshot of the release PR, and the PR changed before it applied the plan. The run before it (41469753494, started at 15:15:14Z) was still updating the same PR until 15:16:41Z.

The `version-pr` job is serialized by its own concurrency group, so I'd expect the two jobs not to overlap. The snapshot most likely went stale while the second run was queued behind the first. That is my inference. The log doesn't show it directly.

The error's own advice is to re-run `callisto release-pr decide` with a fresh snapshot, and the next push's run did that. Re-running the failed run would also have fixed it, since it's the same step with a fresh snapshot.

Nothing needs fixing right now. Trail 158's recovery work (a scheduled `callisto release pending` / drain job) would cover this kind of failure automatically. I'd also add a retry on E148 in the version-pr step there. I haven't touched `release.yml`.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

## Protocol responses (legacy)

If you receive a JSON message with `type: "shutdown_request"` or `type: "plan_approval_request"`, respond with the matching `_response` type — echo the `request_id`, set `approve` true/false:

```json
{"to": "team-lead", "message": {"type": "shutdown_response", "request_id": "...", "approve": true}}
{"to": "researcher", "message": {"type": "plan_approval_response", "request_id": "...", "approve": false, "feedback": "add error handling"}}
```

Approving shutdown terminates your process. Rejecting plan sends the teammate back to revise. Don't originate `shutdown_request` unless asked. Don't send structured JSON status messages — report progress through your task tools if you have them, otherwise in plain prose.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

anyOf.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

<result>Trail 154: I built two of the three planned perf branches. They cut shadcn wall time by about 6% and peak memory by about 5% on this machine. They do not reach the 141 ms / 275 MiB baseline. Neither branch is pushed and no PRs are open. Both commits are GPG-signed (`%G?` prints `G`) and carry the session trailer. The work is in `/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/worktrees/agent-aab89d4ec8820cc42`.

## Branches
| Branch | Base | Tip | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `perf/project-demands-sort` | main (`2daef927`) | `f2ff50c0` | done |
| `perf/module-demands-lean` | `perf/project-demands-sort` | `b508d013` | done |
| `perf/cache-react-augmentations` | main | none | built, measured, deleted |

## Measurements
These are shadcn `extract --json --no-cache` with dependencies loaded. I used the installed shadcn corpus in sibling worktree `agent-a9b87f2da7f20385f`, read-only. Each row is the median of interleaved runs. I could not measure uncontended: the machine's load average was 9–15 throughout, so only compare numbers measured side by side.

| Build | Wall | Peak RSS | Internal `durationMs` |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 171–177 ms | 329–333 MiB | 138–147 |
| `sort` | 161–167 ms (-10 ms) | 332 MiB (unchanged) | 123–130 |
| `lean` | 162–175 ms (within noise of `sort`) | 312–315 MiB (-17 to -20 MiB) | 128–130 |

- **Extract output:** identical across all builds once the changing `durationMs` field is stripped. Without stripping, the hashes differ between runs of the same binary.
- **`just bench`** (Mantine and Chakra, dependencies off, `lean` tip against `origin/main`): Mantine 73 → 75 ms (1.03×), Chakra 65 → 65 ms (1.00×). RSS ratios are 1.01 and 0.99, inside the script's 1.10 time / 1.20 memory thresholds.
- **Baseline gap:** against the same-machine main numbers the two branches give about -6% time and -5% RSS. The 141 ms / 275 MiB baseline was measured uncontended, so the remaining gap is about +14% on memory and an unmeasurable amount on time.

## What each branch does
- **`sort`:** a file's demands all share the same `from` path, so the derived `Ord` compared a long path first on every comparison. They are now sorted by (specifier, name).
- **`lean`:** two changes.
  - **Resolve once per scope:** a module-only import is resolved once per resolution scope (nearest ancestor with `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `jsconfig.json` or `node_modules`). On shadcn, 2748 module-only demands become about 1316 resolutions.
  - **Scan without keeping the parse:** the React-augmentation search no longer keeps a full parse of files it only passes through. The package entry is still parsed in full. A file that cannot declare into React is read for its re-exports only, or skipped if it has none. Any file mentioning `declare module "react"` or `namespace React` still gets a full parse.

## Verification
- **Tests and lint:** full nextest passes (1033, 1 skipped; run unsandboxed because the watch/pty tests need it). The lint suite (fmt, clippy, doc-check, typos, machete) is clean.
- **Real-tree check:** I compared the new re-export scan against `parse_file` on 131,197 real `.d.ts` files from shadcn's `node_modules`, with 0 mismatches. That run found and fixed a missing `export default <import>` case. I also ran the two text prefilters over the same files; the first run found false negatives (`export default <import>`) and after the fix there are none. I then removed those throwaway tests.
- **Changed test:** the existing assertion that a scan-only file is kept in the layer's parse map (`augmentation_tests.rs`) now asserts it is not kept.
- **Changesets:** one per branch, both patch.

## Decisions for you
- **`cache-react-augmentations` dropped.** `merged_interfaces` costs about 14 ms thread-summed per 60k calls on main, roughly 0.25 µs per call, so under 2 ms of wall time. My cached version cost more (33 ms thread-summed, from lock contention). The earlier 5.5 ms estimate came from disabling the lookup entirely, not from making it cheaper.
- **`lean` is a memory win, not a time win.** Time is within noise of `sort`. Keep it only if the memory saving and fewer resolutions are worth about 410 added lines. The scope key assumes directories with the same scope resolve a bare specifier alike. It could be wrong where a `tsconfig` `references` list picks a config by `include`.
- **No dependency parse cache.** I measured instead of prototyping. A warm run with the persisted dependency index is 158 ms against 164 ms for `--no-cache`, only about 4% faster. The acceptance target is `--no-cache`, so a parse cache cannot help it, and it would touch ADRs 0003, 0008 and 0011.
- **Remaining cost:** loading dependencies still costs about 70 ms and 175 MiB on shadcn (164 ms / 313 MiB with, 95 ms / 139 MiB without). Getting back to the baseline needs a bigger change than these two branches.

content.text:
Trail 154's two branches are up as draft PRs #284 and #285 (stacked on #284). They do not meet the trail's goal: shadcn is not back to the baseline of 141 ms and 275 MiB.

On the same machine, the pair cuts wall time about 6% and peak memory about 5%. The machine was busy (load 9–15), so only side-by-side comparisons are meaningful. Extract output is identical. The full test run, lint and `just bench` passed on the worker's branch, but I haven't read the CI checks on the PRs.

- **#284** `perf/project-demands-sort`: about 10 ms less wall time, memory unchanged.
- **#285** `perf/module-demands-lean`: about 17–20 MiB less memory, time within noise. It adds about 410 lines, so it's your call whether that memory win is worth it.
- **Dropped:** `perf/cache-react-augmentations`. The lookup costs under 2 ms of wall time, and the worker's cached version was slower. The plan's 5.5 ms estimate came from removing the lookup entirely.
- **Parse cache:** I'm not pursuing it. A warm run is only about 4% faster than `--no-cache`, which is the trail's target, so a cache can't close the gap.
- **Remaining cost:** loading dependencies still costs about 70 ms and 175 MiB on shadcn. Getting back to the baseline needs a larger change, which I can scope as a follow-up if you want it.

`t158-release` (trail 158) is still running. I'll start `oracle/three-tools-report` and trails 155 and 156 after the earlier PRs merge.

## Branches (stacked, each off the previous, tree clean)

| Branch | Base | Tip |
|---|---|---|
| `feat/release-github-releases` | `main` (2daef927) | `d215c66e` |
| `feat/release-binaries-attestations` | `feat/release-github-releases` | `88dfde0a` |

Worktree: `/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/worktrees/agent-a146a303a3da7d99b`. No release was running when I started.

## Answers to the open facts

- **The signer name is hard-coded.** `RELEASE_COORDINATOR_WORKFLOW_PATH = ".github/workflows/callisto-release.yml"` in Callisto 0.16.0, `crates/callisto-model/src/release/github.rs:148`. `release --dry-run --format json` shows all five slots with that path. I renamed `release.yml` with `git mv` and updated every reference (`callisto.toml`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/adr/README.md`). The workflow's `name:` is unchanged.
- **Homebrew tap keys on tags, not Releases.** `CONTRIBUTING.md:98` says the tap's `brew bump` finds the `npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` tag with `livecheck` and builds from source. Tag names are unchanged and both `cargo/` and `npm/` CLI tags exist for 0.8.0 and 0.9.0. The tap lives in another repo and I couldn't read its config. If it uses `:github_latest`, it would start seeing the new Release.
- **`github-release` needs no slots.** `publish-to` on `cargo/caliper-docgen` alone creates and publishes a Release. Notes come from the `## x.y.z` section of `crates/cli/CHANGELOG.md`.
- **`[release]` needs `github-release` on the product package** (E197), so branch 1 had to come first.

## Surprises that shaped branch 3

- **Enabling `github-release` makes 0.9.0 look unfinished.** `callisto release pending` lists it as missing its GitHub Release. Without `--from`, the command stops with E166 on an older release whose decision no longer decodes. I pinned `RELEASE_PENDING_FROM=2daef927` (the 0.9.0 release commit).
- **The first run after branch 3 merges backfills 0.9.0.** It rebuilds the five binaries from 0.9.0's release commit, attests them, and creates its GitHub Release. Callisto's docs say it adopts the crates, npm packages and tags that already landed. This path has never run, so watch that run.
- **No `schedule:` in Callisto's own example.** I added a daily run (05:23 UTC) anyway, because the same candidate job handles it. On a schedule with nothing unfinished it only refreshes the release PR.

## What changed

- **`callisto.toml`:** `publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]` on the CLI. The `[release]` section sets `product-package = "cargo/caliper-docgen"` and `forge-repository = "orin-dx/caliper"`. Five `[[release.artifact]]` entries use `caliper-docgen-<target>.tar.gz`. Windows is also `.tar.gz`.
- **`callisto-release.yml`:**
  - `plan`: gains `--artifact-repository`, a relative-path intent hash and a `has_artifacts` output, replacing the zero-slot assertion.
  - `build`: tars, attests (`actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475…`) and uploads each asset.
  - `assemble`: new job that writes the artifact manifest.
  - `execute`: gets `attestations: read` and the manifest flags.
  - `release-candidate`: now uses `release pending`.
  - `drain`: new job that dispatches the next unfinished release.
  - `version-pr`: gated on `drain`.
  - Receipt artifacts are named per attempt.
- **`ci.yml`:** the changesets dry-run gets a read-only `GH_TOKEN`.
- **`docs/releasing.md`:** new; covers the flow, outputs, checks, recovery (`ArtifactAssetDiffers`, E180, E140, E148) and a rehearsal checklist.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`:** the Releases text now covers the GitHub Release.

No changeset was added; none of this is consumer-visible code.

- `actionlint` and `zizmor --offline` are clean on all workflows.
- `typos` and `oxfmt --check` pass on the changed files.

Trail 158 is up as three stacked draft PRs: #286, #287 on top of it, and #288 on top of that. None of it has run against a real release, and I haven't read the PRs' CI checks yet.

Callisto is already at its latest version, 0.16.0, so no upgrade was needed. The PRs adopt the Callisto features we weren't using:

- **#286, GitHub Releases:** one Release per CLI version, with notes taken from `crates/cli/CHANGELOG.md`. Tag names are unchanged.
- **#287, binaries and attestations:** the five CLI binaries are attached to the Release, each with a build attestation, and `execute` verifies them before upload. `release.yml` is renamed to `callisto-release.yml`. The worker confirmed Callisto 0.16.0 hard-codes that path as the attesting workflow, and verification fails without it.
- **#288, recovery:** `release pending` finds any unfinished release, a drain job releases the next one, and a daily schedule runs at 05:23 UTC. I'd drop the schedule if you want to stay strictly with Callisto's own example, which has none.

The worker's checks passed: `actionlint` and `zizmor` are clean, and Callisto's `status --check` and `release --dry-run` accept the config. It plans five uploads.

- **Homebrew tap:** It lives in another repo and I couldn't read it. If it uses `:github_latest` instead of tags, it will see the new Release.
- **Rehearsal:** `docs/releasing.md` has a checklist for a trial run on a scratch repo first.
- **E148 race:** I added no retry. Re-running the failed job, or the daily run, covers it.

1. #280 and #281
2. #282 and #283

4. #286, #287 and #288

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

The macOS 14 runner image is set to retire on November 2, 2026, which is today.

- **Official notice:** GitHub's changelog says the image will be retired on November 2, 2026. It covers the `macos-14`, `macos-14-large`, and `macos-14-xlarge` labels. The macOS 14 runner image will be retired on November 2, 2026.
- **Brownouts:** Before retirement, jobs on macOS 14 were set to fail temporarily during scheduled windows, starting October 5, 2026. GitHub also warned that reduced capacity could lengthen queue times. Per the changelog, the last listed window was October 29–31.
- **Migration targets:** GitHub's changelog doesn't name replacements in the excerpt I retrieved. A third-party write-up suggests macos-15-xlarge or macos-26-xlarge as the migration target for the large instance. A 2025 GitHub changelog recommended updating workflows to use macos-14 or macos-15, but that advice predates the macOS 14 retirement. Check the runner-images repository for current labels.
- **Source caveat:** The endoflife.ai page describes the image as having already reached end of life on this date, which is a loose description given the retirement is happening today. The SmartScope article is secondary, so I'd rely on the GitHub changelog for the date.

content.text:
No, we don't have to adjust. GitHub retires the macOS 14 runner image today (2026-11-02). Our workflows never pin it: the only macOS label we use is `macos-latest`, in the two Darwin rows of the release build matrix. That label now resolves to macOS 26 on arm64, per GitHub's [runner-images README](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/README.md) and the [retirement notice](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-01-github-actions-macos-14-runner-image-retirement). Both Darwin builds run on that arm64 host, and the x86_64 build is a cross-compile. The last release run, #269, built both on `macos-latest` and passed.

The latest runner labels from the README:

| OS | Labels |
|---|---|
| macOS 26 | arm64: `macos-latest`, `macos-26`, `macos-26-xlarge`. Intel: `macos-26-intel`, `macos-26-large` |
| macOS 15 | arm64: `macos-15`. Intel: `macos-15-intel` |
| macOS 14 | deprecated: `macos-14`, `macos-14-large` |
| Ubuntu | `ubuntu-latest` is 24.04; `ubuntu-26.04` is the newest |
| Windows | `windows-latest` is Server 2025 |

Our other runners are `ubuntu-latest` (24.04) and `windows-latest` (Server 2025), and both are current.

The one risk is that `macos-latest` can move to a newer image with notice. The binaries are cross-built, so that only matters if the Xcode or SDK version changes the output. If you want deterministic release builds, pin `macos-26` in the matrix. I haven't changed anything.

I'm still waiting on you for the PR merges in the order I gave earlier, and I'm ready to start trails 155 to 157.

## 1. `feat/parity-detail-report`

**Files:** `packages/storybook/scripts/storybook-parity.mjs`, `docs/storybook-parity.md`. There is no changeset, since it only touches a script and docs.

**What changed:** The report now sorts each disagreement into deliberate differences and ones for review. The review items are listed by story and prop in the Markdown, and in full in the JSON.

**Checks:** The formatter and `typos` are clean. `oxlint` doesn't cover `scripts/`.

**Degraded-rate discrepancy:** The docs are right for their commit. Building `e31ccb27` (main through #155) and running the same harness gives 42.1% (797/1892) for shadcn and 27.4% (68/248) for antd, matching the docs and its 13,244 props. Shadcn's "Cannot find the component…" went 382→75, "cannot be used as a component" 344→1, and unexpanded-reference warnings 197→15. I did not bisect which change did what. Props listed also grew from 13,244 to 392,427, so the rates measure different amounts of work.

- `docs/rdt-coverage.md` and a patch changeset.

**What changed:**
- `typeof X` over a literal const (`const SHOW_PARENT = 'SHOW_PARENT'`, imported or declared in a `.d.ts`) now resolves to the literal.
- `keyof typeof X` over a const object literal is now the union of its keys. A spread or computed key stays opaque, and `keyof` of anything else stays opaque.

$T

Four of trail 155/156's five branches are up as draft PRs #295–#298, stacked in order against `main`. All the commits are signed, and the worker's local gate passed on each (1033–1044 tests, lint, typos and machete clean). I haven't read CI on the PRs.

- **#295 and #296:** React component types are matched by import source (`R.FC`, aliased `FC`). An alias of a component declared later in the file now resolves. #296 deliberately reverses the old spec rule that a forward reference must not match, and the test was rewritten.
- **#297:** This branch was added to trail 155. The plan blamed the 211 noise skip notes on alias order and import source, but they come from all-caps constants like `MENU_OPTIONS`. It removes exactly 211 notes (antd 48, shadcn 163), and extracted components are identical.
- **#298:** It adds antd `Option` and shadcn `ChartLegend` ×4 and `Form`, and shadcn is a little faster. The new rule has only 14 detections on these corpora. All 14 are components, but a model labelled them and no human has checked them, so the 95% precision gate is not established. The PR says so.
- **Recall target:** The ~95% antd recall target isn't reachable from this stack. Component counts on antd and shadcn are unchanged apart from the additions above.

The worker is now on the last two branches, `feat/factory-results` and `feat/cross-file-render-evidence`. I told it to stop and report if a branch fails the precision gate or the cost budget. The shadcn `IconLucide` family needs a rule for calls with no type arguments, so it may come back as "out of reach".

Merge order for the stacks (bottom-up, each only after its parent has landed, to avoid another stranded merge):
- #295, then #296, then #297, then #298.
- #289 and #290 are the first priority, since they unblock `oracle/three-tools-report` and `feat/agent-eval-weekly`.

Open PRs now: #289, #290 (the two re-opened ones), #292–#298, plus the release PR #291. The Release & Publish runs on `main` are still queued or in progress; I haven't looked at their outcome.

content.text: I'm starting a read-only adversarial review across three dimensions. Each reviewer works in its own worktree off `origin/main` and has to back every finding with code, a command or a measurement, and try to refute its own claims. A separate verifier re-checks the top findings afterwards.

input.prompt: READ-ONLY adversarial review of the caliper repo (Rust workspace: crates/core, cli, binding (NAPI), semantic, tsc-client; TS packages under packages/, apps/oracle). Do not edit tracked files, commit, push, or open PRs. First `git fetch origin` (sandbox off for git/gh) and `git checkout --detach origin/main` in your worktree so you review current main. Focus: ARCHITECTURE and the SEMANTIC MODEL. Read ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/architecture/*, docs/adr/*, AGENTS.md first, then the code. Hunt for: crate/module layering violations and cycles; the pipeline (extractor -> resolver -> output) boundaries and where responsibilities leak; invariants documented in docs/architecture or ADRs that the code does not enforce (or violates), and ADR claims that are stale or contradicted by code; the semantic model (PropType/types/collected, canonical output interning, layers/members, SourceData and CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION discipline, schema versioning ADR 0017) for representable-illegal-states, lossy conversions, stringly-typed fields, duplicated concepts, and ambiguities between batch/lazy/watch sessions and the optional TS 7.1 semantic backend; public API surface of each crate (what is `pub` that should be `pub(crate)`, leaky types, semver hazards, NAPI boundary and panic containment ADR 0005); dead or redundant code; god modules/functions (report line counts); error-handling architecture. Be adversarial: assume the docs are lying and verify against code. For every finding try to REFUTE it before reporting (search for the counter-example, read callers, run the thing). You may run read-only commands (cargo check/clippy/doc, grep, `cargo tree`, `cargo machete`, wc) but avoid long benchmarks and keep to ONE full cargo build (other workers share the CPU). Report format, a flat list of findings each with: ID (ARCH-n), severity (high/medium/low), confidence (CONFIRMED = you reproduced or read the exact code, PLAUSIBLE = inferred), evidence (file:line and/or command + output excerpt), why it matters, concrete recommendation (what to change, where, effort S/M/L, risk), and how it was verified. Then: what you checked and found sound (so it is not re-litigated), and what you could not verify. Keep total under ~2500 words. No Markdown tables.
